anchor: Bounded-exhaustive set of defense-specific leaking execution graphs
comment: No evaluated enumeration reached UNSAT; every testset stops at max_instances (100k), and Sec. V's OTB paragraph says the shape is 'not reached within its instance cap'. Fig. 3 calling the output 'bounded-exhaustive' contradicts the paper's own results.
proposed: "Minimal leaking execution graphs, up to the bound and instance cap" (or keep 'bounded-exhaustive' only if a run reaches UNSAT; decision D2).
evidence: BIGFIG_FACT_AUDIT.md rows 7, 9 and D2; STAGE1_alloy/models/MANIFEST.md (100k cap); results.tex sec:bug-otb 'does not reach this shape within its instance cap'.

anchor: Stages~1 and~1.5 use Alloy to enumerate minimal leaking execution graphs from the defense's specification.
comment: The caption calls Stage 1.5's output minimal, but the figure itself says Stage 1.5 loosens minimality (slab 2'). Also, per the fact audit, Stage 1.5 is an STT-only prototype that produced none of the reported results, and neither the figure nor the caption says so.
proposed: Stage~1 uses Alloy to enumerate minimal leaking execution graphs up to a bound; Stage~1.5 (prototype, not used for the results below) re-enumerates with loosened minimality, pinned to each Stage~1 graph.
evidence: Fig. 3 slab '2'. Loosened minimality requirements'; BIGFIG_FACT_AUDIT.md row 10 and decision D1 (no campaign used Stage 1.5).

anchor: Blue marks defense-specific components.
comment: The caption explains only blue. It never explains the tan, lavender and light-red slabs 3a-3c (which carry the same meaning as in the graph figures), the dashed 'Same as Stage 1' ghost slabs, the + and prime marks, the numbered chevrons, or the dashed 'SimSpect goal' arrow.
proposed: Blue marks defense-specific components; slabs 3a-3c use the speculation (tan), protection-set (lavender) and transmitter (red) colors of the graph figures; dashed slabs are unchanged from Stage 1, + marks an added and ' a changed constraint.
evidence: p.4 Fig. 3 render; VISUAL_LANGUAGE.md CURRENT RULES (pipeline 3a tan, 3b lavender, 3c light red).

anchor: Non-invasive harness: pipeline-stage probes;
comment: 'Non-invasive' (also in the caption) overstates the harness: the directives change prediction and timing on purpose (BTB force, resolve stall, fnc stall). The 'selects hooks' arrow from transmission mechanisms into the harness has no code behind it.
proposed: "+ Minimal harness (defense logic untouched): probes; speculation and timing directives"; drop the 'selects hooks' arrow, or label it 'design time'.
evidence: BIGFIG_FACT_AUDIT.md rows 30 and 39, decisions D6 and D8; pipeline.tex gem5-hooks paragraph describes the stalls as active control hooks.

anchor: and an inspector checks the defense's transmission criteria
comment: The naming is inconsistent: Fig. 3 says 'Inspector' and 'Pipeline info artifact', while the text and the Fig. 7 caption say 'checker', 'per-transmitter pipeline predicate' and 'gem5 execution trace'. Stage 1 is 'Abstract test generation' and Stage 1.5 'Abstract test enumeration', which implies a difference that does not exist.
proposed: Use one name for the checker across Fig. 3, Fig. 7 and the text, and 'Pipeline trace' for the artifact; e.g. Stage 1 'Minimal-graph enumeration', Stage 1.5 'Graph expansion'.
evidence: Fig. 3 vs Fig. 7 caption ('How the checker decides') and pipeline.tex Transmission Requirement; BIGFIG_FACT_AUDIT.md rows 1, 35.

anchor: inputs \evt{inreg}, \evt{inaddr}, \evt{inmem}; outputs
comment: Five captions say the graphs are 'in the notation of Table I', but Table I gives only the Alloy names (inreg, inaddr, ...). It does not give the drawing notation the graphs use: 'out <- in', [r] for an address, ? for an unspecified operand, r/m tokens, italic flag words, the thick leak path, and the lavender and tan fills.
proposed: Add a row 'Drawn as: out <- in; [r] address; ? unspecified; flags as italic words; thick arrows = leak path; lavender = protected state; tan band = speculative rows'.
evidence: Table I (p.4) vs Fig. 2, 4, 5, 8, 9 rows; captions of Fig. 5, 8, 9, 10 and Table II cite 'the notation of Table I'.

anchor: Only the defense block (speculation contract, protection set, leakage function) differs between models.
comment: The defense components have different names in different places: Table I and Fig. 3 say 'speculation contract' and 'leakage function', while Sec. III and the Fig. 2 caption say 'execution contract' and 'leakage contract'. Table I also sets flags in typewriter (resolved, committed, xmit), but every graph prints them as italic words.
proposed: Pick one pair of terms (decision a1/a2 in FIGURES.md glossary) and use it in Table I, Fig. 2, Fig. 3 and model.tex; set flags in Table I in italics as the figures do.
evidence: model.tex enumerate (Leakage contract / Execution contract); dataflow_8pt caption 'STT's execution contract', 'leakage contract'; Fig. 3 slabs 3a, 3c; FIGURES.md Glossary (a1), (a2).

anchor: Figure \ref{tab:execvocab} contains the execution graph syntax.
comment: This prints 'Figure I'; the target is a table.
proposed: Table~\ref{tab:execvocab} contains the execution-graph syntax.
evidence: p.4 left column, last line of the Execution Syntax paragraph.

anchor: the transmitter load in \texttt{I3} has an address dependency on the load in \texttt{I1}
comment: The text names the instructions I1, I2, I3 in typewriter, but Fig. 2 now labels them i1, i2, i3.
proposed: ... the transmitter load i3 has an address dependency on the load i1 through the ALU op i2 ...
evidence: p.4 text vs Fig. 2 row labels.

anchor: and i3--i5 are speculative (tan band) because branch i2 is unresolved
comment: Branch flags are inconsistent across the graph figures. Fig. 4, 6, 8, 9 and Table II write 'unresolved' on the branch row; Fig. 5 (i2) and Fig. 10 (i2) write nothing; Fig. 2 puts it only in the note column. Captions of Fig. 5, 6 and 10 also use subscripts ($f_0$, $r_0$, $r_1$) where the figures print f0, r0.
proposed: Write the italic 'unresolved' flag on every unresolved branch (Fig. 2 i0, Fig. 5 i2, Fig. 10 i2), and use r0/f0 without subscripts in the captions.
evidence: Renders p.4-p.11; VISUAL_LANGUAGE.md CURRENT RULES ('Resolution status ... shown only on branches and stores'; 'write r0, not $r_0$').

anchor: so Alloy does not synthesize them in its initial pass
comment: Panes (a) and (b) are removed by RO and RI, but the evaluated models run with RR+RC+RS minimality only (RO and RI are off). The production enumeration would therefore emit (a) and (b), and the caption claims the opposite.
proposed: Say that RO/RI are optional clauses, off in the evaluated models (so only (c) is excluded there), or redraw (a)/(b) as RS/RC examples. This depends on decision D4 (Stage 1 minimality).
evidence: STAGE1_alloy/models/MANIFEST.md ('Minimality relaxations ON: RR + RC + RS; OFF: RI + RO'); STT_6.als:301-309 gen_useful_litmus; OTB_GENERATION_GAP.md pitfall 0.

anchor: Pane~(c) also marks load i1 unresolved, which makes concretization do extra work to specify store-set aliasing for it.
comment: Pane (c) puts 'unresolved' on a Load, which breaks the rule that resolution is shown only on branches and stores. The reader is never told that an unflagged load (pane d) counts as resolved. The caption also leaves the dashed rf edge in (b) unexplained.
proposed: Add: 'Non-branch rows without a flag word are resolved and uncommitted; dashed = a removed edge.'
evidence: Fig. 4 p.5 render; VISUAL_LANGUAGE.md CURRENT RULES.

anchor: which is speculative only under the older branches i0 and i1
comment: The figure marks i0 and i1 as committed, so c0 (placed after them and before i2) is not speculative at all under STT's contract. As drawn, the merge has only one tainted source, and the caption's getOldestTaint mechanism cannot occur. The OTB gadget needs the injected load under a branch that is resolved early but still uncommitted.
proposed: Mark i0/i1 'resolved' instead of 'committed', or explain as Fig. 6 does that i0 is committed only at the observation time and resolves at a swept time.
evidence: Fig. 5 p.6 render (i0, i1 'committed'); OTB_GENERATION_GAP.md 'What OTB needs' (ld_inj under br_r, a resolved branch that resolves early); STT_6.als speculation_contract_p.

anchor: Stage~2 interleaving makes a two-source merge that no Stage~1 instance contains.
comment: The paper makes two different claims about the same shape. Fig. 5 and pipeline.tex say no single Alloy instance can contain or express it; Sec. V (OTB) says the bounded enumeration only fails to reach it within its instance cap. The repo shows the shape is SAT when forced.
proposed: "...a two-source merge that the capped Stage 1 enumeration did not produce." and reword pipeline.tex 'which no single Alloy instance can express' to match.
evidence: pipeline.tex Interleaving and State Assignment; results.tex sec:bug-otb; OTB_GENERATION_GAP.md TL;DR (forcing otb_shape is SAT).

anchor: while the test in Figure~\ref{fig:ddi-rf} does not trigger leakage on a model of STT
comment: This sentence says the Fig. 2 test does not leak on STT, while the Fig. 2 caption says it violates STT. It cites Fig. 5 as the example of the Stage-1.5 'overlapping interleaving' round, but Fig. 5 shows the Stage 2 (concretization) round, and Fig. 5 attributes the leak to ReCon, not STT.
proposed: Say 'does not leak on the gem5 implementation of ReCon-STT' and move the Fig. 5 citation to the Interleaving and State Assignment subsection, or add a Stage-1.5 example.
evidence: p.5 'Overlapping interleaving' text vs Fig. 2 caption and Fig. 5 caption ('Stage 2 interleaving', 'ReCon getOldestTaint').

anchor: (2) i0 resolves after i4 executes: violation
comment: The graph violates STT's leakage predicate under both options; what changes is whether a getOldestTaint defense releases i5. Labeling only option 2 'violation' (in red) conflicts with the meaning of 'violation' in Sec. IV and with Fig. 2.
proposed: "(1) i0 resolves before i4 executes: ReCon holds i5" / "(2) ... after: ReCon releases i5 (bug)".
evidence: Fig. 6 p.7 render; pipeline.tex violation definition; Fig. 6 caption ('the run commits without violating the contract').

anchor: on a defense that keeps only an ALU result's oldest taint, such as ReCon (Fig.~\ref{fig:otb})
comment: Fig. 6 and Fig. 10 draw the same gadget (per the source comment) in different ways: Branch_n vs Branch_x, r2 <- r1,r0 vs r0 <- r1,r0, protected m1 vs m0 with no protection mark. Fig. 10's caption calls i1 'speculative under branch i0' while marking it committed, without Fig. 6's explanation.
proposed: Draw Fig. 10's graph with Fig. 6's kinds, names and protection mark, or say in Fig. 10's caption that i0/i1 are committed only at the observation time (as in Fig. 6).
evidence: Fig. 6 (p.7) vs Fig. 10 (p.11) renders; resolutiontiming.tex header comment 'the same two-branch merge shape'; RESULTS_FIGURES.md §7 ('m0 is not gray').

anchor: the committed window closes when fnc retires at 261
comment: Fig. 7 draws the window from lc retire to the branch's resolution, and the text gates on branches still unresolved at the transmission. Fig. 8 draws the window to fnc retire. Fig. 8's packet (cycle 79) comes after its branch resolves (77), so under Fig. 7's rule and the post-fix checker the race is not a violation. The two adjacent figures contradict each other (ties to pending R1, beyond the existing window-name note).
proposed: Settle R1, then draw one window in both figures. If the race stays, label it 'transmission after resolution, before squash' in Fig. 8 rather than putting it in the committed window.
evidence: Fig. 7 p.8 'Unresolved window' ends at 5007 (resolves); Fig. 8 p.10 window to 261; RESULTS_FIGURES.md §2 'Window caveat'; check_ld.py:110-114.

anchor: meets InvisiSpec's criterion before xmit is squashed, so the test is reported as a violation
comment: The paper's one worked example of the violation decision is an InvisiSpec UV1 L1D eviction. The results section calls this a collateral channel outside InvisiSpec's own guarantee. A reader is told the canonical example is a violation, then that it is not one.
proposed: Use an in-scope example (e.g. an STT or SpecLFB load reaching the cache in-window), or caption it as 'reported as a hit; for InvisiSpec this eviction is a collateral channel outside the defense's guarantee (Sec. V)'.
evidence: results.tex fig-todo bullet 'InvisiSpec ... collateral channels sit outside the defense's own guarantee'; FIGURES.md 'Defenses out of scope'.

anchor: N: dispatch\quad E: execute\quad C: complete
comment: The trace figures do not share a visual vocabulary. Fig. 7 uses F/D/E (E = issue), Fig. 8 N/E (E = issue), Fig. 9 N/E/C (E = execute); gem5's own O3PipeView shorthand uses n for rename and p for dispatch. Fig. 7's window is tan-filled, while Fig. 8 and 9 use a white box. In grayscale, Fig. 7's tan window and blue criterion box become the same light gray.
proposed: Use one letter set across Fig. 7-9 (e.g. F fetch, D dispatch, I issue, C complete) and one window style (tan fill + frame) in every trace figure.
evidence: Renders p.8, p.10, p.11 (color and -gray); /Users/annaeaton/Downloads/dockerrecon/gem5-recon/util/o3-pipeview.py:192-213.

anchor: (STT build with commitToIEWDelay $=4$, test inst-047231)
comment: The caption gives only commitToIEWDelay=4, but the run used se_slowcomm.py, which also sets iewToCommitDelay=30, squashWidth=1 and back/forwardComSize=40, plus a 150-cycle fnc commit stall. fnc (i1) is not drawn, though the window ends at its retirement. Separately, the figure marks E (issue) at 49, while the caption and text say i5 issues at 78.
proposed: Name the full slow-comm configuration and the fnc stall; add an fnc row or say fnc = i1; label 49 'ready (held)' rather than E.
evidence: wiki/findings/bug/stt_slowcomm_vp_squash_race/provenance.json (se_slowcomm_hardcoded, fnc_commit_stall_cycles 150); results.tex race example paragraph.

anchor: and $r0$ is the address of both the store i4 and the transmitter i5
comment: The store i4 is drawn as '? <- [r0]', the same form as a load, so the graph never shows that i4 writes memory. No edge reaches i4's address, so the forwarding that the bug is about appears only in the trace.
proposed: Draw the store as '[r0] <- ?' and add to the caption: 'the store's address shares r0 by state assignment; the model has no store-to-load edge, so forwarding appears only in the trace'.
evidence: Fig. 9 p.11 render; FIGURES.md 2026-11-03 note (no store-to-load memory edge in inst-014912.xml).

anchor: lc, fnc: last committed, first uncommitted
comment: Table II says 'first uncommitted' where the text and Fig. 7 say 'first non-committed', and it adds an 'uncommitted' flag word that Table I does not define. The 'Target transmitter' row covers only Branch_x and Other_x (calling the latter 'Divide'), so readers cannot see that Load/Store transmitters need no special handling, or that Other_x is a divide or zero-skip multiply.
proposed: Use 'first non-committed'; add to row 5: 'Load, Store: no special code'; say 'Other_x (divide)'.
evidence: Table II p.6 render; plans/fig_d_instrtable.md Row 5 (kinds: load, store, branch, zsm/divide).

anchor: no existing method {\mdseries\itshape (this work)}
comment: 'no existing method (this work)' reads as if this work were the missing method's absence. The caption does not explain the three arrow styles (solid proof, thick dashed '?' gap, thin dashed prior work) or the blue fill.
